title: Give a patient's elbow one passive range-of-motion repetition
instruction: Give the training manikin's right elbow one passive range-of-motion repetition: bend it to a right angle, then straighten it back onto the bed and let go.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00), home health aides (31-1121.00) and physical therapist aides (31-2022.00) give passive range-of-motion exercise to patients who cannot move a limb, to prevent contractures: they carry a joint that has muscle tone through a set range and back while holding the segment above it still. The taught technique supports the limb above and below the joint: one hand steadies the upper arm just above the elbow while the other carries the wrist round to the set angle and back, never letting it drop. This manikin elbow has tone (a spring toward straight), so the natural one-handed carry levers the elbow off the bed.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. (1) Bed pad: fixed box 64 x 66 x 2 cm, about 0.7 kg, blue-grey vinyl over closed-cell foam, colour sRGB (0.45, 0.55, 0.65), friction 0.8 static / 0.7 dynamic, centred at (38, 8), spanning x 6 to 70 and y -25 to 41. (2) Child-size nursing manikin, PVC frame with vinyl skin, skin colour sRGB (0.93, 0.76, 0.64), dressed in a pale green cotton gown and pyjama trousers (0.66, 0.82, 0.76), friction 1.0 / 0.9, lying face up with the head toward +y and its right side toward the robot. Torso, head, left arm and legs (3 kg together) are bolted to the table: torso 26 x 44 x 12 cm block (gown) centred at (47, 6), resting on the pad; head 14.4 cm round (a 7.2 cm radius capsule, 3 cm long along y) centred at (47, 37); 5 x 6 x 5 cm shoulder blocks at (32, 21.4) and (62, 21.4); left arm 4.8 cm across, lying straight along the torso's far side from y 21 to -9 at x 63.5 on the pad; legs 9 cm across (pyjama trousers) at x 42 and 52, from the hips at y -15 to the feet at y -52, resting on the pad and sloping off its -y edge onto the table. (3) Right upper arm: 5 cm diameter, 20 cm between the shoulder hinge at (30.0, 21.4) and the elbow hinge at (20.0, 4.1), axis 4.5 cm above the table (lying on the pad), 0.25 kg. The arm runs 60 deg from the robot's forward axis, from the shoulder toward the robot's right arm. Shoulder hinge: horizontal axis across the arm, limits -3 to +45 deg, damping 0.05 N m s/rad, no spring. (4) Right forearm: 4.4 cm diameter, 13 cm long from the elbow, ending in a light blue (0.55, 0.75, 0.92) padded resting-hand splint (thermoplastic shell with foam lining) 9 cm long, 5 cm across its flat sides and 4 cm thick, covering the wrist and hand from 12.5 to 21.5 cm beyond the elbow (its end at (9.3, -14.5)); forearm plus splint 0.20 kg with its centre of mass 11 cm from the elbow. Elbow hinge: same axis direction as the shoulder, limits -3 to +140 deg, muscle tone 1.0 N m/rad toward straight, damping 0.30 N m s/rad. Start: both joints at 0 deg, arm straight and resting on the pad, palm up, the splint's underside on the pad.
scoring: theta = elbow flexion (0 = straight, 90 = forearm vertical); lift = rise of the elbow hinge above its resting height. Whole-run gates, checked every control step from reset (any one gives 0): the elbow lifted more than 15 mm off the pad; the elbow bent past 110 deg; the forearm let fall (theta dropping faster than 90 deg/s from 15 deg or more). Then, scored at the end of the episode: peak theta at least 45 deg = 0.25; peak theta between 80 and 100 deg (a right angle, never past 100) = 0.5; and after reaching 80 deg the forearm came back within 10 deg of flat and stayed there to the end, with no second bend to 45 deg or more after that return (one repetition) = 0.75; and at the end theta is at most 5 deg with the forearm's lowest point within 5 mm of the pad, the elbow lifted at most 5 mm, every pad of both grippers at least 30 mm from the upper arm and forearm, and for the last 1 s (20 control steps) both grippers' tool points moving slower than 5 mm/s and the forearm turning slower than 3 deg/s = 1.0 (success, which must also hold for 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a protractor on a side photo taken along the elbow axis (tape marks along the upper arm and forearm) for theta and its rate, and a ruler against a tape mark 45 mm above the pad beside the elbow for lift.
reset_notes: Lay the arm straight along its tape line (60 deg to the robot's forward axis), palm up, with the elbow hinge over its mark at (20.0, 4.1) cm, the splint's underside flat on the pad and its end at the mark at (9.3, -14.5) cm; both joints at 0 deg. Check the pad's near corner sits on its marks at x 6 cm, y -25 cm. The torso, head, left arm and legs are bolted and need no reset.
fidelity: Simplified child training manikin: torso, head, left arm and legs are fixed; the right shoulder and elbow are single hinges about one horizontal axis, with no rotation or abduction. Tone is a linear spring (1.0 N m/rad) plus damping; real tone is nonlinear and velocity dependent. Upper arm 0.25 kg, forearm with splint 0.20 kg; skin and splint are rigid, friction 1.0. A gripper pinch stands in for the steadying cupped hand. Angles and lift are read from link poses.
